I generally avoid discussing the forum with new players.  I think they already find it intimidating when I pull out my playmat, bags full of dice and tokens, and three containers of cards (the Core box, and two white card boxes containing Shattered Timelines and playtest cards).  It can be even more over new players' heads if they see me pull up Spiff's Randomizer on top of all of that!

I generally try to approach rules in a scholarly sense, if I may be so bold.  I think understanding the intentions behind the rules helps illuminate what game GtG was trying to create.  There is certainly more to it than playing however you want to, but there's nothing wrong with that, either.  Christopher can't be in the room of every single Sentinels game in the world to be consulted over rules nuances in his game (sadly).  I just find it fascinating to learn how a certain mechanic was intended to be used for this game.  I usually love it, and sometimes I hate it.  But every time I've had a rule clarified I've used it without feeling that the game becomes "imbalanced" or "broken".

The balance between an author's intent and the reaction to that author's creation makes a work interesting for me.  Discussing and sometimes arguing or debating rules on this forum helps me understand how this game came to be what it is, and I find that experience to be absolutely incredible.
